\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{अलीकडे} (alīkaḍe)}{अलीकडे (alīkaḍe)}]{\mr{अलीकडे} (alīkaḍe) — recently}

\label{lesson:MR-C159-alikade}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for to obtain, then the Marathi for to save.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{अलीकडे}}
\textbf{\mr{अलीकडे}} — \emph{alīkaḍe} — \textquotedblleft{}recently\textquotedblright{}. Marathi's past ends in \textbf{-\mr{ले}}, \textbf{-\mr{लो}} or \textbf{-\mr{ली}}: \textbf{\mr{अलीकडे} \mr{मी} \mr{एक} \mr{पुस्तक} \mr{वाचले}.} — \emph{alīkaḍe mī ek pustak vācle} — \textquotedblleft{}Recently I read a book.\textquotedblright{}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{अलीकडे}} (\emph{alīkaḍe}) is \emph{alī-}, \textquotedblleft{}this side\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{-\mr{कडे}}, \textquotedblleft{}toward\textquotedblright{}. The origin of \emph{alī-} is not settled; CDIAL has no entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{alīkaḍe}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marathi for to obtain, then the Marathi for to save, then say \emph{alīkaḍe} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{पूर्वी} (pūrvī)}{पूर्वी (pūrvī)}]{\mr{पूर्वी} (pūrvī) — formerly, before}

\label{lesson:MR-C159-purvi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for to save, then the Marathi for recently.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{पूर्वी}}
\textbf{\mr{पूर्वी}} — \emph{pūrvī} — \textquotedblleft{}formerly, before\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\mr{पूर्वी} \mr{इथे} \mr{एक} \mr{दुकान} \mr{होते}.} — \emph{pūrvī ithe ek dukān hote} — \textquotedblleft{}There used to be a shop here.\textquotedblright{} \textbf{\mr{होते}} is the past of \textbf{\mr{आहे}}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{पूर्वी}} (\emph{pūrvī}) is Sanskrit \emph{pūrva}, \textquotedblleft{}fore, first, ancient\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8343), with the ending \emph{-ī}: \textquotedblleft{}in former times\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{आधीच} (ādhīc)}{आधीच (ādhīc)}]{\mr{आधीच} (ādhīc) — already}

\label{lesson:MR-C159-adhic}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for recently, then the Marathi for formerly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{आधीच}}
\textbf{\mr{आधीच}} — \emph{ādhīc} — \textquotedblleft{}already\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\mr{आधी}}, \textquotedblleft{}before\textquotedblright{}, with the emphatic \textbf{\mr{च}}: \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{आधीच} \mr{जेवलो}.} — \emph{mī ādhīc jevlo} — \textquotedblleft{}I have already eaten.\textquotedblright{} A woman says \textbf{\mr{जेवले}}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{आधीच}} (\emph{ādhīc}) is \textbf{\mr{आधी}}, \textquotedblleft{}before\textquotedblright{}, with the emphatic \textbf{-\mr{च}}. The origin of \textbf{\mr{आधी}} is not settled: neither CDIAL nor DEDR has an entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{भूतकाळ} (bhūtkāḷ)}{भूतकाळ (bhūtkāḷ)}]{\mr{भूतकाळ} (bhūtkāḷ) — the past}

\label{lesson:MR-C159-bhutkal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for formerly, then the Marathi for already.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{भूतकाळ}}
\textbf{\mr{भूतकाळ}} — \emph{bhūtkāḷ} — \textquotedblleft{}the past\textquotedblright{}. It is \textbf{\mr{भूत}}, \textquotedblleft{}what has been\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{\mr{काळ}}, \textquotedblleft{}time\textquotedblright{}. Grammar books use it for the past tense too.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{भूतकाळ}} (\emph{bhūtkāḷ}) is a Sanskrit compound, a tatsama: \emph{bhūta}, \textquotedblleft{}become, been, past\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9552), and \emph{kāla}, \textquotedblleft{}time\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 3084), with Marathi \textbf{\mr{ळ}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{घडणे} (ghaḍṇe)}{घडणे (ghaḍṇe)}]{\mr{घडणे} (ghaḍṇe) — to happen}

\label{lesson:MR-C159-ghadne}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for already, then the Marathi for the past.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{घडणे}}
\textbf{\mr{घडणे}} — \emph{ghaḍṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to happen\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\mr{काय} \mr{घडले}?} — \emph{kāy ghaḍle} — \textquotedblleft{}What happened?\textquotedblright{} Its past is \textbf{\mr{घडले}}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{घडणे}} (\emph{ghaḍṇe}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited from Sanskrit and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{ghaṭate}, \textquotedblleft{}is busy with; happens\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4407).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{मी} \mr{गेलो} (mī gelo)}{मी गेलो (mī gelo)}]{\mr{मी} \mr{गेलो} (mī gelo) — the past, one small ending at a time}

\label{lesson:MR-C159-gelo}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{\mr{घडणे}}, \textquotedblleft{}to happen\textquotedblright{}, then \textbf{\mr{मी}}, \textquotedblleft{}I\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\mr{जाणे}}, \textquotedblleft{}to go\textquotedblright{}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: who did it?}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{काल} \mr{मी} \mr{पुण्याला} \mr{गेलो}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāl mī puṇyālā gelo.} — \textquotedblleft{}Yesterday I went to Pune.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

The past shows who did it. A man says \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{गेलो}}; a woman says \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{गेले}}. With \textbf{\mr{तो} / \mr{ती}}, use \textbf{\mr{तो} \mr{गेला} / \mr{ती} \mr{गेली}}. With respect or several people, use \textbf{\mr{तुम्ही} \mr{गेलात}}. Hear the same gender endings you already know from \textbf{\mr{माझा} / \mr{माझी} / \mr{माझं}}, now after \textbf{-\mr{ल}-}.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a few useful stems}
Most verbs put \textbf{-\mr{ल}-} onto the stem: \textbf{\mr{बसणे} $\to$ \mr{बसलो}}, \textbf{\mr{झोपणे} $\to$ \mr{झोपलो}}, \textbf{\mr{पडणे} $\to$ \mr{पडला}}. Two everyday verbs change more: \textbf{\mr{येणे} $\to$ \mr{आलो} / \mr{आली}} and \textbf{\mr{होणे} $\to$ \mr{झाला} / \mr{झाली}}. Put \textbf{\mr{नाही}} after the completed form for \textquotedblleft{}did not\textquotedblright{}: \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{गेलो} \mr{नाही}}.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}Yesterday I went to Pune\textquotedblright{} — \emph{kāl mī puṇyālā gelo} or \emph{gele}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}She came home in the evening\textquotedblright{} — \emph{tī sandhyākāḷī gharī ālī}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}We sat. We slept.\textquotedblright{} — \emph{āmhī baslo. āmhī jhoplo.}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}I went\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{गेलो}}, or \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{गेले}}.) \textquotedblleft{}He went\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\mr{तो} \mr{गेला}}.) \textquotedblleft{}She came\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\mr{ती} \mr{आली}}.) \textquotedblleft{}I did not go\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{गेलो} \mr{नाही}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{त्याने} \mr{काम} \mr{केलं} (tyāne kām kelaṁ)}{त्याने काम केलं (tyāne kām kelaṁ)}]{\mr{त्याने} \mr{काम} \mr{केलं} (tyāne kām kelaṁ) — who did it, and what was done}

\label{lesson:MR-C159-tyane-kela}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}I went\textquotedblright{}, then the \textbf{-\mr{ने}} that can mean \textquotedblleft{}by\textquotedblright{}, then \textbf{\mr{करणे}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: -\mr{ने} on a past doer}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{त्याने} \mr{काम} \mr{केलं}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tyāne kām kelaṁ.} — \textquotedblleft{}He did the work.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

With a past action done to something, the third-person doer takes \textbf{-\mr{ने}}: \textbf{\mr{तो} $\to$ \mr{त्याने}}, \textbf{\mr{ती} $\to$ \mr{तिने}}, \textbf{\mr{मीरा} $\to$ \mr{मीराने}}. The first and second person stay \textbf{\mr{मी}} and \textbf{\mr{तू}} in ordinary Marathi: \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{काम} \mr{केलं}}.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: the verb follows the object}
The ending now follows what was acted on: \textbf{\mr{त्याने} \mr{आंबा} \mr{खाल्ला}}, because \textbf{\mr{आंबा}} is masculine; \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{पोळी} \mr{खाल्ली}}, because \textbf{\mr{पोळी}} is feminine; \textbf{\mr{त्याने} \mr{पुस्तक} \mr{वाचलं}}, because \textbf{\mr{पुस्तक}} is neuter. So \textbf{\mr{त्याने} \mr{कुत्रा} \mr{पाहिला}} has \textbf{\mr{पाहिला}} following masculine \textbf{\mr{कुत्रा}}.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I ate a chapati\textquotedblright{} — \emph{mī poḷī khāllī}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}He saw a dog\textquotedblright{} — \emph{tyāne kutrā pāhilā}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}She read a book\textquotedblright{} — \emph{tine pustak vācalaṁ}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}He did the work\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\mr{त्याने} \mr{काम} \mr{केलं}}.) Does \textbf{\mr{मी}} take \textbf{-\mr{ने}} here? (No.) Which ending follows \textbf{\mr{पोळी}}? (\textbf{-\mr{ली}}: \textbf{\mr{खाल्ली}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{होता} / \mr{होती} / \mr{होते} (hotā / hotī / hote)}{होता / होती / होते (hotā / hotī / hote)}]{\mr{होता} / \mr{होती} / \mr{होते} (hotā / hotī / hote) — was, were, was not}

\label{lesson:MR-C159-hota}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}I went\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}he did the work\textquotedblright{}, then the present \textbf{\mr{आहे}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{होता}, \mr{होती}, \mr{होते}}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{तो} \mr{घरी} \mr{होता}. \mr{ती} \mr{घरी} \mr{होती}. \mr{ते} \mr{घरी} \mr{होते}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{to gharī hotā. tī gharī hotī. te gharī hote.} — \textquotedblleft{}He was, she was, they were at home.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

The past of \textbf{\mr{आहे}} agrees like an adjective: masculine \textbf{\mr{होता}}, feminine \textbf{\mr{होती}}, neuter or respectful/plural \textbf{\mr{होते}}. With a place, say \textbf{\mr{गावात} \mr{एक} \mr{नदी} \mr{होती}}, \textquotedblleft{}There was a river in the village.\textquotedblright{}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{नव्हता}}
\textquotedblleft{}Was not\textquotedblright{} joins the negative into the past form: \textbf{\mr{तो} \mr{शाळेत} \mr{नव्हता}}, \textbf{\mr{ती} \mr{शाळेत} \mr{नव्हती}}, \textbf{\mr{दुकान} \mr{मोठं} \mr{नव्हतं}}. Keep the same agreement ending.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}There was a river in the village\textquotedblright{} — \emph{gāvāt ek nadī hotī}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}He was not at school\textquotedblright{} — \emph{to śāḷet navhtā}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}They were at home\textquotedblright{} — \emph{te gharī hote}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}She was\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\mr{ती} \mr{होती}}.) \textquotedblleft{}He was not\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\mr{तो} \mr{नव्हता}}.) \textquotedblleft{}I went\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{गेलो} / \mr{गेले}}.) \textquotedblleft{}He did the work\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\mr{त्याने} \mr{काम} \mr{केलं}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
